title: CHAPTER THIRTY-EIGHT. On the sin of the human being
latin: CAPUT TRIGESIMUM OCTAVUM, De hominis peccato. HActenus de statu post lapsum et libertate: sequitur peccatum. Peccatum est transgressio legis divinae, seu defectus a lege Dei tanquam norma rectitudinis (1 Ioh. 3:4; Rom. 4:15). II. Estque primum aut a primo ortum. III. PRIMUM est transgressio legis de non comedendo de arbore scientiae boni et mali, a protoplastis in paradiso commissa (Gen. 3). Hoc peccatum vocatur peccatum originans, quia ab eo ortum duxit peccatum originale in posteris et omnia actualia.
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-EIGHT. On the sin of the human being.

Thus far concerning the state after the fall and liberty: next follows sin. Sin is the transgression of the divine law, or a falling short from Gods law as the norm of uprightness (1 John 3:4; Romans 4:15). II. And it is either the first or sprung from the first. III. The FIRST is the transgression of the law concerning not eating from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, committed by the first parents in paradise (Genesis 3). This sin is called originating sin, because from it original sin in posterity and all actual sins took their rise.

title: IV–V. Original sin: imputed guilt and inherent corruption; habitual deformity
latin: IV. Peccatum originale est vitium naturae nostrae ab Adamo derivatum, constans reatu et corruptione. Reatus est obligatio ad mortem aeternam propter Adami peccatum nobis imputatum (Rom. 5:12-19). Corruptio est privatio iustitiae originalis et habitus pravus in intellectu, voluntate, affectibus totoque homine. V. HABITUALE est deformitas obiecti a rectitudine legis, manens in natura etiam quando actus non exseritur. Hinc infantes etiam ante actuale peccatum reatu et corruptione tenentur (Psal. 51:7; Iob 14:4; Eph. 2:3).
english: IV. Original sin is the fault of our nature derived from Adam, consisting of guilt and corruption. Guilt is the obligation to eternal death because of Adams sin imputed to us (Romans 5:12-19). Corruption is the privation of original righteousness and a crooked habit in intellect, will, affections, and the whole human. V. HABITUAL sin is the deformity of the object from the uprightness of the law, remaining in the nature even when the act is not put forth. Hence infants even before actual sin are held by guilt and corruption (Psalm 51:7; Job 14:4; Ephesians 2:3).

title: VI. Notable points on original sin: imputation, propagation, and extent
latin: VI. Sunt autem hic quaedam NOTANDA. 1. Peccatum Adami imputatur posteris non sola imitatione, sed reali communicatione reatus, quia omnes in Adamo tanquam in capite et radice fuerunt (Rom. 5:12). 2. Propagatio fit per generationem naturalem, non per creationem animae tanquam peccatricis a Deo. 3. Peccatum originale non est substantia, sed accidens privativum et positivum habitus mali. 4. Non tollit liberum arbitrium quoad actus naturales, sed privat viribus ad bonum spirituale. 5. Baptismus et regeneratio non auferunt totam corruptionem in hac vita, sed reatum et dominationem peccati (Rom. 6-7).
english: VI. Certain points are here to be NOTED. First, Adams sin is imputed to posterity not by imitation alone, but by a real communication of guilt, because all were in Adam as in a head and root (Romans 5:12). Second, propagation happens through natural generation, not through creation of the soul as sinful by God. Third, original sin is not a substance, but a privative accident and a positive habit of evil. Fourth, it does not take away free choice as to natural acts, but deprives of powers toward spiritual good. Fifth, baptism and regeneration do not remove all corruption in this life, but the guilt and dominion of sin (Romans 6-7).

title: VII–XII. Actual sin: definition, kinds against the law of works, and omissions
latin: VII. ACTUALE peccatum a Scholasticis et Theologis dicitur omnis actus, sive interior sive exterior, dissonans a lege Dei. Distinguitur in peccata commissionis et omissionis; in peccata cordis, oris, et operis; in peccata contra Deum, proximum, et seipsum. XII. Peccatum contra legem operum est transgressio praeceptorum moralium Decalogi et legis naturae. Peccatum omissionis est neglectus debiti officii. Communicatio cum peccatis alienis etiam peccatum est, quod veteres his versiculis expresserunt: Consulo, praecipio, consentio, provoco, laudo, non retego culpam, non punio, non reprehendo, non obsto, sed praecipio et defendo aliena.
english: VII. ACTUAL sin is called by the Scholastics and theologians every act, whether inward or outward, dissonant from Gods law. It is distinguished into sins of commission and of omission; into sins of heart, mouth, and work; into sins against God, neighbor, and oneself.

XII. Sin against the law of works is the transgression of the moral precepts of the Decalogue and of the law of nature. Sin of omission is the neglect of a due office. Communication with others sins is also sin, which the ancients expressed in these verses: I counsel, I command, I consent, I provoke, I praise; I do not uncover the fault, I do not punish, I do not rebuke, I do not withstand, but I command and defend anothers sins.

title: XVI–XXI. Sins in necessities and adiaphora; sins of infirmity, ignorance, and malice
latin: XVI. Peccatum in necessariis est, vel contra praecepta affirmativa vel negativa quae absolute obligant. XVII. Peccatum in adiaphoris est, quando res per se mediae fiunt malae ex circumstantia scandali, contemptus, aut malae intentionis (Rom. 14; 1 Cor. 8-10). XXI. Peccatum infirmitatis est, quando ex imbecillitate naturae aut subita passione peccatur, non ex destinata malitia. Distinguitur a peccato ignorantiae, quod ex defectu debitae cognitionis oritur, et a peccato malitiae seu praesumptionis, quod ex deliberata voluntate contra cognitam legem committitur. Peccatum in Spiritum Sanctum est obstinata et malitiosa repudiatio cognitae veritatis, cui remissio in hoc saeculo denegatur (Matth. 12:31-32; Heb. 6:4-6; 10:26-29).
english: XVI. Sin in necessities is either against affirmative or negative precepts that oblige absolutely. XVII. Sin in adiaphora is when things in themselves indifferent become evil from the circumstance of scandal, contempt, or bad intention (Romans 14; 1 Corinthians 8-10).

XXI. Sin of infirmity is when one sins from weakness of nature or sudden passion, not from destined malice. It is distinguished from sin of ignorance, which arises from defect of due knowledge, and from sin of malice or presumption, which is committed from deliberate will against a known law. Sin against the Holy Spirit is obstinate and malicious repudiation of known truth, to which remission is denied in this age (Matthew 12:31-32; Hebrews 6:4-6; 10:26-29).

title: XXIV–XXV. Sin against conscience and not against conscience; Cap. 38 close
latin: XXIV. Peccatum contra conscientiam est, quando quis agit contra dictamen conscientiae rectae vel erroneae — nam etiam erronea, donec corrigatur, obligat ad non agendum contra eam (Rom. 14:23). XXV. Peccatum non contra conscientiam est, quando actus obiective malus committitur absque actuali contradictione conscientiae, sive ex ignorantia sive ex induresciente consuetudine. Actualia peccata non solum ea sunt quae fiunt ex contumacia, destinata malitia, et indurata peccandi consuetudine, sed et quae committuntur ex infirmitate et ignorantia, nec tantum committendo, sed et omittendo vel aliorum peccatis communicando. De permissione peccati sequenti capite agendum.
english: XXIV. Sin against conscience is when someone acts against the dictate of conscience, whether right or erroneous — for even an erroneous conscience, until corrected, obliges one not to act against it (Romans 14:23). XXV. Sin not against conscience is when an objectively evil act is committed without actual contradiction of conscience, whether from ignorance or from a hardening habit.

Actual sins are not only those that happen from stubbornness, destined malice, and an hardened custom of sinning, but also those committed from infirmity and ignorance — and not only by committing, but also by omitting or by communicating with others sins. Of the permission of sin the following chapter must treat.
